newsitem.title: UK: BAe says Matra missile merger now completed.
newsitem.headline: BAe says Matra missile merger now completed.

text.p: LONDON, Nov 4 (REUTER) - British Aerospace Plc said on Monday it has completed the agreement with France's Lagardere to merge the two group's guided missile businesses, following governmental and regulatory approvals.

A company spokesman said the final agreement was signed last week and the companies would now get on with setting up the new corporate structure for Matra BAe Dynamics, with two head offices, in London and Paris.
"It's all approved and it was signed in Paris last Thursday," a company spokesman said.

BAe and Lagardere said in announcing the initial agreement in August that the deal would create Europe's largest guided weapons business with annual sales of some 1.0 billion stg, a 2.6 billion stg order book and combined workforce of 6,000.

Industry sources say it remains to be seen whether it will draw Europe's other missile businesses into a broader coalition in the slow movement towards consolidation of the European defence and aerospace industries.
Last month the French government picked Lagardere as preferred bidder for Thomson SA.

The proposal has hit widespread controversy in France but if it goes ahead Lagardere has vowed to merge the Thomson CSF defence business with its own unit Matra and then invite other European firms to join in creating pan-European defence groups.
BAe and Lagardere have already agreed that Matra BAe Dynamics would absorb Thomson's guided missile business.
